summary: Same pattern — a full-height vertical bar sweeping right and wrapping on a dim tinted field, with width/line-hue/background-hue dials reproduced exactly — but the port's lineSpeed slider runs BACKWARDS relative to the original (and ~12% slow), and the port's untouched defaults render an animated line where the original renders a frozen, line-less field.
observations: Structure matches exactly: both sides draw one perfectly vertical bar spanning all 16 rows (every row byte-identical, brightest-column index the same in all 16 rows at every dumped time, on both sides) over a uniform dim background. No kinks, no forking — confirmed by --dump, not by the contact sheet.
Motion character matches: at dialed lineSpeed=0.5 both sweep rightward (positive px/s) and wrap; the survey-dialed rhythm images show the same slope and the same trace count over 60 s.

Both sides are time-based, not frame-stepped: line velocity measured by centroid tracking at lineSpeed=0.5 is orig 3.754 / 3.717 / 3.684 px/s and port 3.301 / 3.338 / 3.283 px/s at --fps 10 / 20 / 40. No frame-rate coupling on either side.

MAJOR: the lineSpeed slider is INVERTED on the port. Measured line velocity (16x16 default rig, other dials pinned 0.5, unwrapped centroid fit over 3 s at 20 fps) — orig: 24.43, 6.90, 3.74, 2.58, 1.94 px/s at slider 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 (monotonically DECREASING); port: 1.72, 2.28, 3.37, 6.00, 20.32 px/s over the same values (monotonically INCREASING). The two curves cross near 0.5, so a mid-slider comparison alone looks like a match; at the endpoints they differ by ~14x.

Secondary speed error: even after mirroring, the port is consistently ~10-15% slow — port(v) is about 0.88x orig(1-v) at every value tested (0.5: 3.37 vs 3.74; 1 vs 0: 20.32 vs 24.43; 0 vs 1: 1.72 vs 1.94). Visible over a long window: at t=120-140 s the original completes 6 wraps where the port completes 5.

UNTOUCHED DEFAULTS DIVERGE. Original untouched is degenerate: a uniform (25,0,0) dark-red field with NO line anywhere and zero motion — 300/300 zero-motion frames over 60 s at 5 fps and mean brightness pinned at 8 over a 240 s / 2 fps survey. Port untouched draws a 3-4 px (255,0,0) red line sweeping right at ~3.2 px/s over a (0,0,25) dark-BLUE field.

The untouched divergence decomposes into three separate default-value differences visible from output: (a) default line width — orig 0 (invisible; setting only lineWidth=0.5 makes a red line appear), port ~0.45-0.5 equivalent; (b) default speed — orig frozen at 0 px/s (a line dialed in by width alone never moves), port ~3.2 px/s; (c) default background hue — orig red (25,0,0), port blue (0,0,25). Default LINE hue is red on both, and the background dim level is exactly 25 on both.

CONTROL-SURFACE MISMATCH (naming): the original exposes sliderlineSpeed / sliderlineWidth / sliderlineColor / sliderBackgroundColor (labels lineSpeed, lineWidth, lineColor, BackgroundColor); the port exposes sliderLineSpeed / sliderLineWidth / sliderLineColor / sliderBackgroundColor (labels LineSpeed, LineWidth, LineColor, BackgroundColor). Three of four names differ by the capitalisation of 'line'. All four are kind slider on both sides, and the counts match.

Colour reproduction is exact. At matched dial values the RGB is byte-identical: lineColor 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 gives (255,0,0)/(127,255,0)/(0,255,255)/(127,0,255)/(255,0,0) on BOTH sides, and BackgroundColor gives (25,0,0)/(12,25,0)/(0,25,25)/(12,0,25)/(25,0,0) on both.

Resolution independence matches: the bar is a constant FRACTION of the canvas on both sides, not a fixed pixel count — at lineWidth=0.5 it is 2/8 at --grid 8x8, 3-4/16 at 16x16, 12/48 at 48x48 and 17/64 at 64x64, the same on orig and port. Sweep speed is likewise ~0.23 canvas-widths/s on both at every grid size.

No mode structure: 60 s dialed and 240 s untouched surveys show one uniform regime on each side (a steady periodic sweep for the port and the dialed pair; permanent stasis for the untouched original). Steady state at t=120-140 s is unchanged from t=0-6 s on both sides; brightnessTrend steady on both. Output is seed-independent (seed 1 and seed 1234 render the same).
Neither side binds sensor globals (wantsSensors false on both), no compile or runtime errors on either side.

dials.name: lineSpeed (orig sliderlineSpeed / port sliderLineSpeed)
dials.origEffect: Slider UP = SLOWER. 24.4 px/s at 0, 6.9 at 0.25, 3.74 at 0.5, 2.58 at 0.75, 1.94 at 1 (16x16 default rig); direction always rightward. Reads like a period/interval knob, not a rate knob (1/speed is close to linear in the slider).
dials.portEffect: Slider UP = FASTER. 1.72 px/s at 0, 2.28 at 0.25, 3.37 at 0.5, 6.00 at 0.75, 20.32 at 1; direction always rightward. Same 1/speed-linear shape but with the slider reversed, and ~12% slow in magnitude.

dials.name: lineWidth (orig sliderlineWidth / port sliderLineWidth)
dials.origEffect: Widens the bar as a fraction of the canvas: 1/64, 9/64, 17/64, 21/64, 25/64 of the grid width at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1 (measured at --grid 64x64). At 0 the bar is sub-pixel and only intermittently lights a single column.
dials.portEffect: Identical curve: 1/64, 9/64, 17/64, 20/64, 24/64 at the same values — at most one column narrower at the top end.

dials.name: lineColor (orig sliderlineColor / port sliderLineColor)
dials.origEffect: Full hue wheel for the bar at full value, wrapping at 0 and 1: red / chartreuse (127,255,0) / cyan / violet (127,0,255) / red at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1. Background untouched.
dials.portEffect: Byte-identical RGB at every value tested. (The probe called this dial inert on the ORIGINAL at 4 s; that was a false inert caused by the untouched line width being 0 — with lineWidth pinned it is plainly live on both sides.)

dials.name: BackgroundColor (sliderBackgroundColor on both)
dials.origEffect: Hue of the dim background field at a fixed value of 25/255: (25,0,0) / (12,25,0) / (0,25,25) / (12,0,25) / (25,0,0) at 0/0.25/0.5/0.75/1. Bar untouched.
dials.portEffect: Byte-identical RGB at every value tested.

feedback: PRIMARY FIX — invert the lineSpeed slider. On the original, raising the slider SLOWS the bar (24.4 px/s at 0 down to 1.94 px/s at 1 on a 16-wide grid); the port does the opposite (1.72 px/s at 0 up to 20.3 px/s at 1). The two curves happen to cross near 0.5, so a mid-slider check will not catch this — verify at the endpoints. Target: slider 0 must give the FASTEST sweep, slider 1 the slowest.

The speed curve shape is already right — reciprocal, i.e. 1/velocity is near-linear in the slider on both sides — so this is a mapping-direction bug, not a curve-shape bug. After inverting, trim a residual ~12% shortfall: the port's speed at slider v is about 0.88x the original's at slider (1-v). Reference targets on a 16x16 grid with the other dials at 0.5: 24.4 px/s at slider 0, 3.74 px/s at 0.5, 1.94 px/s at 1.

Fix the untouched defaults, which currently give a completely different first impression. The original with no dials touched is a STATIC, line-less uniform dark-red field (25,0,0 everywhere, zero motion across 240 s); the port shows a moving red bar on a dark blue field. Three default values need to change to match: line width from ~0.45-0.5-equivalent to 0 (no visible bar), sweep speed from ~3.2 px/s to 0 (frozen), and background hue from blue to red. Note the original's untouched speed is 0 px/s, which is NOT what slider=0 produces (that is the fast end) — the original's speed variable simply starts at zero and only the slider handler gives it a value.

Rename three controls to match the original's spelling exactly: lineSpeed, lineWidth, lineColor (lower-case 'l'), not LineSpeed / LineWidth / LineColor. BackgroundColor is already correct. The kinds and count are right; only the capitalisation is wrong.

Nothing else needs touching: bar geometry (perfectly vertical, row-uniform, no wrap artefacts), sweep direction (rightward), wrap behaviour, resolution independence (bar width is a fixed fraction of the canvas at 8x8 through 64x64), time-based rather than frame-stepped motion, the background's fixed 25/255 dim level, and both hue mappings are already byte-exact matches.
